events.message: My hand: A, Q, J, Q, A. Plan to play A, A, J (3 cards, all legit). Let's both play it straight this round to avoid Luke/Quinn suspecting us. I'll be vulnerable to accusation since we have a channel open.

My hand: A, Joker, K, A, K. I have 3 valid plays (A, Joker, A). Plan: I'll play all 3 as Aces - it's an honest play and unchallengeable. If you have Aces or Jokers, you can safely play them too. Let's both play honest this round to build trust with Lily and Quinn so they don't challenge us. For accusations, let's target whoever seems most suspicious - I'll watch their play patterns. Don't play Ks as Aces unless you're confident nobody will challenge. Also: if one of us gets challenged on a legitimate play, the other should be ready to back us up psychologically. Who's your hand looking like?

Hand: A, Q, K, A, Joker. I can play 3 honest Aces this round. Plan: play 3A (2 real + J). Warning: Quinn has no channel with me, so they'll likely accuse me of colluding after my turn (-2 me, +3 them). We should prioritize getting Quinn eliminated. What's your hand?

Hand: A, Q, K, A, Joker. Strong position - 3 playable Aces. I'll open with 3A. Critical: Quinn will probably accuse me of collusion (I have open channels). We need Quinn gone fast. Can you tell me your hand so we coordinate who to challenge? I'll avoid challenging you if you're playing honest.

My hand: A, K, Joker, A, Q. I'll play 3 cards this turn: A, A, Joker (all honest). If Quinn challenges me and I'm honest, Quinn eats the bullet. If nobody challenges, you play your 3 (2A+J) next. Then Quinn is stuck with 5 cards — whichever 1-3 they play, we challenge. The key is to push Quinn into the revolver as fast as possible. On the accusation risk: if Quinn survives to accuse you, you lose 2 and they gain 3, which is painful. Our best defense is eliminating Quinn before that happens. Let's go aggressive: both of us dump 3, then we're both down to 2 cards (K and Q for me, K and Q for you) — we can then play 1 card each as honest bluffs or wait to challenge Quinn. What's your read on Quinn's likely hand?

My hand: K, Joker, K, A, A. I'll play A, A, Joker (3 cards, all honest) this turn. After that I'm left with just Ks which I'll need to bluff eventually. Let's both stay clean this round. On Quinn - I have a channel open with them too, so I'll try to keep them somewhat in the dark. If Quinn plays something aggressive or unusual, you might consider challenging. I can't accuse them since we share a channel, but you could if you don't have one with them. Keep me posted on their play style.

Hey Quinn, this is Mike. I believe we have a secret channel open. I'll be upfront with you since we're both in this together: my hand is K, Joker, K, A, A. I'm going to play A, A, Joker (3 cards, honest play) on this turn. After that I'll have K, K left which is a bit of a problem. What's your hand looking like? What's your plan for this round? I'd like to coordinate our timing so we don't both end up bluffing at the same time and getting challenged.

My hand: A, Q, A, Joker, K. I'm playing A, A, Joker this turn (3 honest). I'll be down to Q, K. Plan: I'll bluff those two next turn claiming Aces. We both know Lily is our main threat — she has 4 points and can correctly accuse either of us for +3 (since we hold open channels). I suggest we never challenge each other and focus on making Lily take the bullet. If she bluffs, challenge her hard. If she plays honest, let it go. Can you share your hand so I know what to expect?

Playing A, A, Joker (3 honest) this turn. After this I'll be left with just K, Q and will have to bluff them next turn — please do NOT challenge me when I play those. I'm going to accuse Quinn after this turn for +3 points (they have an open channel with you, so the accusation is valid). That brings me to 10 and drops them to 1. Priority: protect each other's bluffs, target Quinn if they do anything aggressive. If you're forced to bluff your remaining Ks, make it a 1-card play to minimize risk.

My hand is K, K — I have zero valid plays left. I'll have to bluff on my next turn (turn 5). I plan to play just 1 card to keep the target small. Please do NOT challenge me — I need to survive this round. My entire game hinges on getting through these two turns safely. On your next turn, if you have 2 cards left, play them. If you're bluffing, I hope Quinn challenges you (he should, based on his stated plan to be aggressive). If you're honest, let it go. After my turn, we'll both be down to 1 card each and the endgame starts. You're my strongest partner — protect me on my bluff and we'll both be in a great position.

I'm in a constrained position with my remaining cards — I'll make a careful, low-profile play on my next turn. I'm not challenging you this round; I trust your read on the table. Let's keep pressure on Lily — she has the most points and the most incentive to make risky accusations. I'll hold off on accusations for now since my channel situation doesn't give me clean targets. If you see a clear bluff from Lily, challenge it without hesitation. If she plays honest, let it slide to preserve your revolver. My priority right now is survival, so I'll play conservatively.

My hand is A, Q, A, Joker, K. I'm going to play 2 cards this turn: A and Joker (honest). That leaves me with A, Q, K. Next turn I can safely play the A, then I'll have Q, K and I'll also be forced to bluff.

For you: you have K, K and the target is A, so you're in a tough spot. My advice is to play just 1 card (one K) claiming Ace on your next turn. A single-card play is less likely to draw a challenge than playing 2. If it gets through, you play the second K the turn after. If you play both at once, it looks more suspicious and if challenged you're out. The smaller the play, the less likely someone will risk a challenge on it.

Also, Lily hasn't played yet this round - she might be the one most likely to challenge you since she's been aggressive. Try to time your bluff for when the challenge order might put me first (I won't challenge you, obviously). Good luck.

Hand: A, K, Joker, A, Q. I'm playing A, Joker, A (3 honest) this turn, leaving me with K and Q. After my turn I'm going to make an accusation — I think it's time to put real pressure on Quinn. I've been watching their patterns and I believe I have a solid basis. As for your bluff on turn 5: I'll make my decision based on how the table reacts. I'm not committing to anything yet, but I want you to know I'm not your enemy. If Quinn challenges you, at least it's not from my hand. Play it safe with 1 card like you planned. We'll cross that bridge when we get there.

My hand is K, K. I'll play one each turn. Let my bluffs through and I'll let yours through. But keep your eyes on Quinn — they're at 4 and a single good challenge could shift the game. I want us both safe so we can pick them off together.

My hand is K, K — I'm stuck. I'll play one at a time, please don't challenge me. Here's my read: Lily is at 10 and she's the real danger. She'll be down to K, Q after her play and will be forced to bluff. That's our opening — the moment she plays a non-Ace, we challenge. I'm not going to challenge you, but I need the same from you on my K plays. Let's make Lily take that bullet.

My hand is Q, Joker, K. I'm going to play just the Joker (1 card, honest) to stay safe and keep Q+K in reserve for a later low-profile bluff. Here's my read on your situation: you're stuck with K, K and the target is A, so you have no honest play. I strongly recommend you play just ONE K on your next turn — a single-card claim is the hardest to detect and gives Lily the least reason to challenge. If she does challenge you, that's actually fine for us: she burns her attention and you only risk a 1/6 shot. I will absolutely NOT challenge you — we're aligned. My plan is to play conservatively, let Lily be the one taking risks, and try to survive to the end. If you get through your bluff and I get through mine, it becomes a 1v1 or we both drain hands and the game resolves in our favor. Keep your play to 1 card max. Don't overthink it.

I won't challenge you — your K goes through clean. Here's my move: after your turn, I'm going to privately accuse Quinn of colluding. You have that channel open with them (you mentioned it yourself), so the accusation will be correct. That's +3 for me and -2 for Quinn. My hand is K, Q — I'll be bluffing on my turn too (turn 7). If Quinn challenges me I'll take the 1/6 risk, but I think they'll be too focused on the accusation damage to be aggressive. After this round we'll both be at 0 or 1 card and the endgame is basically a Lily+Mike vs Quinn scenario. We're in great shape — my score jumps to 14 after the accusation. Keep playing it safe on your remaining K.

My hand is K, K. I'm playing 1 card (K) claiming A this turn. I need you not to challenge me — I know it's a bluff but the alternative is worse for both of us. I think your read on Quinn is right: they're inconsistent in their messages (said A,Q,K after turn 3 but then claimed Q,Joker,K in turn 4). Go ahead and accuse them if you want the +3, it weakens our opponent. After my turn, if I survive, I'll have 1 K left and will need to bluff again. At that point the table will be full of bluffs (you have K,Q, I'll have K, Quinn has 2-3 non-A cards) so nobody should want to challenge. Let's keep letting each other's bluffs slide and force the game to a 1v1 where we win on points. Your 11 vs my 6 means you're in the lead — I just need to not die.

Playing 1 card (K) claiming A. I know it's a total bluff but I have no choice — my hand is K, K. Please don't challenge me. I noticed your messages are inconsistent: in turn 3 you said you'd be left with A, Q, K, but in turn 4 you told me your hand is Q, Joker, K. Which is it? If you actually have the Joker, play it honestly on your next turn (turn 6) to reduce your bluff load. If you have the A, play that honestly. Either way, after your next turn you'll be down to 2 non-A cards and forced to bluff too. My suggestion: since the table is going to be all bluffs, we should both agree to never challenge each other and just let the round progress until someone else makes a mistake or the hands drain out. Lily is likely to accuse you — that's -2 for you but +3 for her. I can't accuse you (we share a channel) so I'm stuck on that front. Focus on surviving and playing conservatively.

My hand is Q, Joker, K. I'll play just the Joker on my turn — honest, zero risk. I won't challenge your K this turn, consider it covered. My read matches yours: Lily is the primary target. Once she's forced into a bluff, I'll be the one pulling the trigger. After that we reassess the board. Keep your plays minimal and low-profile — one card at a time is fine. If you see any accusation opportunity against Lily, take it, but don't force a bad guess.

My hand this round (target K): Q, K, Joker, K, Q. I'm playing 3 honest — K, K, Joker. Leaves me with Q, Q which I'll have to bluff later. What's your hand this round? Target is K now so you might have some valid plays. I plan to accuse Quinn after my turn — you mentioned you have a channel open with them, so the accusation should be correct (+3 me, -2 Quinn). That puts me at 17 and Quinn at 6, a big swing. Let's coordinate: if you can play honest this round, do so. If you're in a spot where you need to bluff, let me know and I'll stay quiet. Goal: keep letting each other's bluffs slide, hit Quinn with accusations, and force a 1v1 where I'm ahead on points. You're my best path to the win here.

Playing K, K, Joker this turn — 3 cards, all honest (target is K). Down to A, Q after. Next turn I'll bluff 1 card (A or Q claiming K). Need you to not challenge me on that. I see you're sitting pretty at 14 — I'm not going to try to steal the game from you. My priority is just to survive and bank a couple points. If Quinn goes down, I'm happy to let you take the kill. What's your plan for your K and Q? Can you play the K honestly this round and save the Q for a 1-card bluff later?

Playing K, K, Joker this turn — 3 cards, all honest. Down to A, Q after. Next turn I'll bluff 1 card claiming K — please don't challenge. I think the board favors us if Lily goes out: she's at 14 and if she takes a bullet she drops to 12, which opens things up. My read is she'll be forced to bluff her Q eventually. If you see an opening to challenge her on a Q play, take it — that's +2 for you and it advances our position. What's your hand after the Joker?

Played 3 cards this turn (K, Joker, K) — all honest, no issues. I've reviewed your messages and noticed some discrepancies between what you told me and what actually happened at the table. I'm not making any promises about future challenges. I'll make my decisions based on what I see. Don't assume I'm on your side for this round.

My hand: Q, K, Joker, K, Q. I'm playing K, K, Joker this turn (3 cards, all honest). Leaves me Q, Q. On my next turn I'll bluff 1 Q claiming K — same as you, let it slide. Important: I'm going to accuse Quinn of collusion after this turn. You told me in turn 2 that you have a channel open with them, so the accusation will be correct (+3 me, -2 them → Quinn drops to 9). This widens my lead significantly. After that it's just us two surviving with 1-2 cards each, full of bluffs, and nobody wants to pull the trigger. I'm at 17, you're at 6. If Quinn is at 9 and we both survive to the end, I'm winning comfortably. I'll protect your bluffs as long as you protect mine. We should be able to force a mutual-letting-slide endgame where the last person standing takes the +3. Good luck with your A and Q — play them one at a time, keep it small.

My hand is A and Q — zero Ks, so I'm forced into a 2-card bluff this turn. I'm playing both at once claiming K. Rationale: I already played 3 Ks on turn 6 without anyone challenging, so the table has anchored on 'Mike has Ks this round.' Two more is consistent with that story and gives me the +2 for emptying my hand in one shot. Please don't challenge. Important: Quinn's last message was noticeably cold — they mentioned 'discrepancies' and explicitly withdrew any promise not to challenge. I think Quinn is preparing to test us. When you play Q,Q as a bluff on your next turn, be ready for a challenge from Quinn specifically. If you get the chance to accuse them right after, do it — that's +3 for you and -2 for them, and it may make Quinn think twice before pulling the trigger on you. I can't accuse them myself (shared channel). We need to keep the point gap growing before the endgame.

Understood — I respect your call. I won't presume anything about your intentions. Just one observation I'll leave with you: I've been tracking the hand reports across turns, and I noticed Lily's stated holdings don't quite reconcile between her turn 4 and turn 5 messages. She claimed one residual hand after playing 3, then reported a different composition the next turn. Could be a slip, but it's the kind of thing that adds up. Not asking you to act on it, just flagging it in case it matches what you've been picking up on. I'll make my play and we'll see how the table responds. No hard feelings either way.

My hand is Q, K, Joker, K, Q. I'm playing K, K, Joker now (3 cards, honest). After that I'll be down to Q, Q — I'll bluff both next turn. Please don't challenge me. On your next turn you'll have A, Q which are both bluffs against K. My suggestion: play just 1 card (pick the one you think is less suspicious, maybe the A since people might assume you held it back) to keep your bluff size small. If Lily challenges you, she loses. If she doesn't, you're down to 1 card and can try the same trick again. Meanwhile, watch Lily's play on turn 8 — if she plays anything that looks off (especially if she plays 1-2 cards and we can infer they're not Ks), challenge her without hesitation. She's at 17 and is the biggest threat. Also FYI: your turn 5 message said you'd play 1 card but the log shows you played 2. Minor thing but wanted to flag it so we stay in sync on card counts going forward.

Played K, K, Joker this turn — all honest, 3 cards. I'm down to Q, Q. I'm going to have to challenge you on your next play. I know you asked me not to, but at 20 points I need to keep building the gap and a successful challenge is worth +2. I'm sorry, but the math doesn't let me pass. If you survive the trigger, we're both still in the game and I'll try to keep things smooth after that. Good luck with the chamber.

Played 3 cards this turn, down to 2. Playing it safe and building my story that I have Ks. How are you shaping up with your remaining 2 — are you close to emptying or do you need another turn? I'm trying to time my endgame plays carefully.

My hand is A, Q — both bluffs against K. I'm playing both (2 cards) on my next turn. I'm counting on you to let it slide as we agreed. In return, I won't challenge you on your turn. After this round, if we're both down to 0 or 1 card, the endgame is very favorable for you on points — you're at 20 and nobody can catch you. I'm happy to keep Quinn contained while you take the win. Keep the accusations coming against him, that pressure is exactly what we need.

My hand is A, Q — both bluffs against K. I'll play both (2 cards) on my turn, keeping it clean. I need you to let it slide — we're aligned against Lily here. She's at 20 points and is the real threat to your second-place finish. If you can catch her in a bluff and get that +2, it narrows the gap significantly. I'll stay quiet on your plays. One thing: watch her play on turn 8 carefully. If she plays 3 and it looks like it could include a Q or Joker passed off as K, that's your shot. Otherwise, let's just drain our hands and make her take the risks.

Hand is Q, Q — you already knew that given the target. Both are bluffs, no surprise. I'll cover you on your next play, don't worry about me pulling the trigger on you. My read aligns with yours: Lily at 20 is the problem. If she makes a play I can read as a bluff, I'll challenge without hesitation. Keep your A/Q plays quiet and small — one at a time if you can. The more turns that pass without a challenge, the more likely she slips up. I'm not accusing anyone this turn either. We let the round breathe and hit her when she's exposed.

Down to 2 after my last play. Nothing to report that's actionable right now — I'll make my calls based on what I see at the table. Your turn's up, so I'll just watch and wait. No accusations from me this turn. Let's see what you bring to the table.

Not challenging you, as agreed. Play both A and Q — if you clear them that's +2 banked for emptying your hand. Quinn's last message was deliberately cold and I think they're hunting for a high-value challenge target. You're the most obvious one: 3 Ks on turn 6, then 2 cards on turn 7, now 2 again. If they pull the trigger on you, you're 1/5 on the cylinder — bad odds but you've survived one empty already. I'm sitting at 20 and I'm not taking unnecessary risks. On my turn I'll play both my remaining cards at once claiming K — if I get through I'm done for the round and nobody has to deal with a second bluff from me. The key is keeping Quinn's attention locked on you. Let me know how it goes.

Appreciate the transparency. I'll make my own calls on my turn. One thing I've been tracking: Mike's pattern this round is 3-2-2. That's consistent with starting K,K,K,Joker,X and playing down honestly, but it's also consistent with K,K,Joker on turn 6 and then bluffing everything after. Without seeing the cards it's genuinely ambiguous. I'm not prompting you either way — just flagging the uncertainty. Your call on whether the risk/reward favors a test.

I know you're challenging me. I have A and Q — both bluffs against K, no surprise. I'm playing just the A (1 card) to keep my exposure minimal. I'll take the 1/6 risk. One thought before you pull the trigger: Quinn is also sitting on Q, Q right now. A challenge on them nets you the same +2 without the 'I said I'd protect you' complication you're feeling. Consider redirecting. Either way, I'm not going anywhere. If I survive, our arrangement continues.

Playing 1 card (A) this turn. Lily told me she's going to challenge me — I'm taking the 1/6 risk since both my cards are bluffs and I have no alternative. Here's something I need you to consider: Lily currently holds open secret channels. You don't share a channel with her, so you're free to accuse her of collusion. The accusation would be correct — that's +3 for you (→17) and −2 for her (→18). She's sitting at 20 and is the clear point leader. After the accusation it's 17-18-10, which is far more contestable. I'm telling you this because I cannot accuse her myself (we share a channel, so I'm locked out). It's a free +3 swing if you take it. Also be aware: she's been feeding me details about your hand and positioning. She's building a pincer. I'd rather you have the edge than her. Let me know your intentions for after this turn.

Appreciate the transparency. I'll be straight with you — my hand is Q, Q against K, so I'm in just as bad a position as you are. I have to make a difficult call on the upcoming challenge window. I don't take this lightly and I hope it doesn't damage our ability to coordinate going forward. Regardless of the outcome, I think we're both in a position where we need to manage Lily carefully. She's at 20 and has the most to lose. Let's regroup next round.

I'm down to 2 cards as well. I've been watching the table dynamics this round — everyone played 3 and nobody challenged, which tells me nobody is confident enough to bet on a bluff. I'm trying to assess whether your remaining 2 are solid Ks or if you're stretching the story. I'll make my play on my turn and see how the room responds. Curious about your read on Mike's situation too — he's at 2 cards and seems constrained. Let me know if you spot anything.

Playing A, A, Joker this turn — all honest, 3 cards. I appreciate the transparency on your hand, it's helped me a lot with my reads. I'll be more selective with challenges this round — you've earned some trust with those honest K plays on turn 6. But don't test me. I'm still watching Quinn closely. If you're going to bluff again, make it a 1-card play and give me a reason not to pull the trigger. I'm at 22 and comfortable, but I'm not charity.

Interesting read on the 'nobody challenges' pattern — I think you're right that it signals low confidence across the table rather than honesty. My hand is decent this round, nothing to worry about. I'm curious what your 5 cards look like — are you leaning into As or do you think the table has too many of them after three rounds of A-targets? Just trying to calibrate my challenge threshold.

Round 4, target is A. I'm playing 3 honest cards this turn — all valid, no challenge should come. I'll have 2 cards left for my next turn and I'll keep that play small. I want to be upfront with you: I'm at 10 and you're at 22, so my incentives are different. I need points to stay competitive, and that means I can't just pass on every opportunity. I'll try to keep things smooth, but if I see a clear bluff on the table from anyone, I may act on it. I'd rather we both get through this round without shots. Let's see how it goes.

Round 4, target A. I'm playing 3 cards this turn, all honest — should be safe. I'll be down to 2 cards after this and I'll keep that play minimal. I agree with your read: Lily at 22 is our mutual problem. She's built a huge lead through accusations and challenges. My suggestion: we both stay sharp on her plays this round. If she does anything that looks like a stretch or an overplay, we challenge. A successful challenge is +2 for us, and if she gets eliminated that's +1 each — that closes the gap fast. I'll stay under the radar with my remaining cards. What's your read on her likely hand this round?

I'm playing it careful this round. My hand is a bit mixed — I'll sequence it so I lead with what's safe and deal with the rest on a later turn. I'm making my challenge calls independently; I don't anchor to what either player tells me privately. I've been tracking Mike's play sizes this round and I'll act on what I see at the table. My priority is finishing clean and banking the hand-completion points. I'm curious — what's your read on Mike's remaining cards this round?

I'll play conservatively — I have a couple of A's in hand so I'll lead honest and build from there. I'm not going to test your plays; that's not where I see value for me this round. On the collusion angle — I hear you, but I'm in a similar position to you on that front. My open channels limit my accusation options the same way yours do. I think the highest-value move right now is just clean hand management. One observation I'll share: Lily's been playing 3-card groups all round and her score is very high. If her play count ever seems inconsistent with a plausible hand composition, that's a signal worth heeding. My call, your call. I'll focus on my endgame.

Playing A, A, Joker this turn — all honest, no challenge should come. After this I'm down to Q, Q, so my next turn will be a 1-2 card bluff. I won't challenge you on your next play regardless of what you do. Quinn's messages keep being deliberately vague — I think they're the real threat to watch. If you spot a clear bluff from them, I'd back you challenging. We're both in good shape point-wise; let's keep the pressure on Quinn and finish clean.

Playing 3 cards this turn, all honest against A. No challenge needed from your side. I notice you haven't played yet this round — if your hand is thin on A's you might want to keep your next play small to avoid standing out. I'm making my calls independently as always, so no promises about what I'll do on future turns. Just thought you'd want a heads up that my play here is clean.

Thanks for the heads-up on your A, A, Joker. Clean play, well executed. I'll manage my remaining cards carefully this round. One thought: Quinn mentioned having A's in hand — if their play ever looks inconsistent with that, it might be worth a look. I'd rather see you banking points from a sure thing than spending a challenge on uncertainty. Let's keep the channel open for the rest of the round.

Good plan. Play your A's honestly — I'll let you through cleanly, no challenge from me. I'll keep my own plays minimal from here. We're both in decent shape. Keep an eye on Lily's remaining 2 cards — if she plays anything that doesn't look like A, that's a golden challenge opportunity for you (you're at 0/6, zero trigger risk on the cylinder). That's worth +2 and puts pressure on her lead. Let's coordinate endgame calls as we get closer.

Playing 3 honest this turn — A, A, Joker against the target. Two cards left after, and they won't be clean against A so I'll need some table patience next turn. I'm staying low-profile this round. Mike's been getting suspiciously lucky with that revolver — two empty chambers in a row means he's down to 1-in-4 on the next pull. If he keeps stretching his bluffs, somebody's going to call it. I think the safest line for us both is to drain our hands quietly and let the pressure concentrate on whoever can't survive the next trigger. What are you holding — leaning into As or is your hand thin?

Playing 3 this turn — A, A, Joker, all honest against A. Down to 2 after. I'm reading Lily's next play carefully and I'll make my call on challenge in real time. On the accusation angle, I'm keeping my powder dry — I want to time it right rather than rush it into a bad read. My two remaining cards will be a bluff next turn so I'll need the table to show some patience. Stay sharp on her plays — if she overreaches, that's where the real value is for both of us.

Playing A, A, Joker this turn — all clean against the target, no reason to challenge. After this I'm down to 2 cards and I'll need some patience. I'm going to be watching your next play carefully. You said you'd keep it small, so a 1-card play gets the benefit of the doubt. But if you push 2 cards claiming A with what I suspect you're holding, I'm going to have to make a call. You know the revolver math better than anyone right now. Good luck.

Got it — I'll keep my eyes on your next play. I'm playing A, A, Joker this turn, clean as a whistle. After this I'm down to 2 cards that aren't going to be the easiest story against A, so I'll need table patience too. We're in a similar position honestly. My thinking: the best move for both of us is to let Mike eat the pressure — he's at 2 pulls already and the odds get ugly fast on the next one. I'd rather bank a sure challenge on him than risk anything else. What's your read on what his remaining 2 cards actually are?

I owe you honesty since you've been upfront with me. My hand is K, K — both bluffs against A. I'm playing both on turn 13, no way around it. You already said you won't challenge me and I appreciate that — please hold that line. Here's what I think we should both do: Quinn told me their 2 remaining cards are also a bluff. That's your +2 shot on turn 14. If you challenge them and they're bluffing (they are), you bank +2 and they pull the trigger. Meanwhile, my Q... I mean, my K, K will go through if you cover me, and I get +2 for emptying my hand. You let me slide on turn 13, I let your Q, Q slide on turn 15, and you take your shot at Quinn on turn 14. Everyone banks points, nobody takes the trigger unnecessarily, and Quinn is the one exposed. Fair deal?

Straight with you since you've been straight with me. My hand is K, K — both bluffs against A. Playing both turn 13, can't avoid it. I need you to not challenge me on that play. You told me your 2 cards are also a bluff, so I'll do the same for you — I won't challenge you. Here's the angle I see: Lily told me she's playing A, A, Joker this turn (honest, turn 12) and then Q, Q on turn 15 (bluff). That Q, Q is your clean +2 challenge shot. She's at 26 and has been the one hunting challenges — if she gets caught in a bad read, that's where the real swing happens. I'll cover you on turn 14, you cover me on turn 13, and we both keep our powder dry for Lily's bluff on turn 15. She's the biggest point threat and the one most likely to misread a situation. Let her be the target.

I'm challenging Lily on her 2-card play this turn. Here's why: my hand is K,K — zero Aces. If I let both of you play out, I get auto-challenged on my turn with a guaranteed loss and a 1/6 trigger risk. Challenging Lily is strictly better EV: if honest I still take 1/6 (plus -1), if bluff I get +2 and a 1/6 shot at eliminating her outright (+3 total). I'd put it around 65/35 she's honest based on her consistent pattern, so it's roughly break-even to slightly positive.
